docs.title: GrOpt
docs.text:
GrOpt is a toolbox for MRI Gradient Optimization (GrOpT). Rather than analytical combinations of trapezoids, the software uses optimization methods to generate arbitrary waveforms that are (hopefully) the most time optimal solution.

The main workhorse of the package are the optimization routines written in C++, which for final applications are designed to be compiled into a pulse sequence as needed.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
In this simple we generate a flow compensated phase encode, with a known duration (1.12 ms).

gparams = gropt.GroptParams()

# Set up problem
gparams.dt = 10e-6
gparams.N = 112
gparams.vec_init_simple()

# Add constraints
gparams.add_gmax(.08)
gparams.add_smax(200)
gparams.add_moment(0,14.0)
gparams.add_moment(1,0.0)

# Solve
gparams.solve()
out = gparams.get_out()

Which produces the waveform:

from timeit import default_timer as timer

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import gropt
from timeit import default_timer as timer import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import gropt In [3]: Copied! 
# This is an example of the unregularized solution

gparams = gropt.GroptParams()
gparams.N = 101
gparams.dt = 10e-6
gparams.vec_init_simple()

gparams.add_gmax(.08)
gparams.add_smax(200)
gparams.add_moment(0,2.0)
gparams.add_moment(1,0.0)
gparams.add_moment(2,0.0)

start_t = timer()
gparams.solve()
out = gparams.get_out()
stop_t = timer()

print(f'Final Good: {gparams.final_good>0}   Solve time: {1000*(stop_t-start_t):.1f} ms')

TV_norm = np.abs(np.diff(out)).sum()
print(f'||g||_2 = {100*np.linalg.norm(out):.2}  ||Dg||_1 = {100*TV_norm:.2}')

plt.figure(figsize=(6,3))
tt_ms = np.arange(out.size)*gparams.dt*1e3
plt.plot(tt_ms, out)
plt.show()

plt.figure(figsize=(6,3))
plt.plot(tt_ms[:-1], np.diff(out)/gparams.dt)
plt.show()

Adds a moment constraint to the optimization problem.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default order int

The order of the moment. Defaults to 0.

0 target float

The target value for the moment constraint. Defaults to 0.0.

0.0 tol float

The tolerance for satisfying the moment constraint. Defaults to 1e-6.

1e-06 units str

The units of the moment constraint, for target and tolerance Defaults to 'mTms/m'. Can be 'mTms/m', 'Ts/m', 'rads/m', or 's/m'

'mT*ms/m' axis int

The axis along which the moment is calculated. Defaults to 0.

0 start_idx int

The starting index (inclusive) for the range over which the moment is calculated. A value of -1 indicates the beginning of the axis. Defaults to -1.

-1 stop_idx int

The stopping index (exclusive) for the range over which the moment is calculated. A value of -1 indicates the end of the axis. Defaults to -1.

-1 ref_idx int

The reference index, (i.e. index where t=0 in moment calculations), which often could be the time of excitation. Defaults to 0.

0 weight_mod float

A weighting factor for this specific constraint in the optimization problem. Defaults to 1.0.

docs.title: PNS (SAFE-model)
docs.text: PNS parameters can be loaded from an .asc file using the gropt.readasc.asc_to_safe function, which will create a python dictionary that can be used as input to the SAFE constraints. Alternatively, no parameters can be entered to use some default demonstration values. Finally, to get a SAFE predcition, the gropt.get_SAFE function can be used.

asc_to_safe(asc_file: str) -> tuple[dict, dict]

Convert an ASC file to SAFE format.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default asc_file str

Path to the ASC file.

required

Returns:

Type Description tuple[dict, dict]

SAFE hardware parameters. The first dictionary contains the parameters for the PNS model, and the second dictionary contains the parameters for the cardiac model. If the cardiac model is not available, the second dictionary will be None.

Source code in gropt\readasc.py 
def asc_to_safe(asc_file: str) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """
    Convert an ASC file to SAFE format.

    Parameters
    ----------
    asc_file : str
        Path to the ASC file.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, dict]
        SAFE hardware parameters. The first dictionary contains the parameters for the
        PNS model, and the second dictionary contains the parameters for the cardiac model.
        If the cardiac model is not available, the second dictionary will be None.
    """
    asc, extra = readasc(asc_file)

    try:
        hw = asc_to_hw(asc, cardiac_model=False)
        hw_cardiac = asc_to_hw(asc, cardiac_model=True)
    except KeyError as e:
        print(f'ERROR: finding SAFE parameters in asc file. KeyError: {e}')
        hw = None
        hw_cardiac = None

    if hw is not None:
        hw = hw_namespace_to_dict(hw)
    if hw_cardiac is not None:
        hw_cardiac = hw_namespace_to_dict(hw_cardiac)

    return hw, hw_cardiac

docs.title: Defining the problem
docs.text:
The optimization problem is contained in a GroptParams object. This contains descriptors of the waveform desired (size, raster time, nummber of axis, inversions,...). The problem can defined directly using these settings (see TODO: Add Example), or with helper functions, such as:

For more information see here

docs.title: Adding constraints and objectives
docs.text:
The GroptParams object has a range of functions that add constraints.

Available constraints can be seen here

docs.title: Solving
docs.text: Once the problem has been defined, and constraints and/or objective functions added, we solve for a solution with either the GroptParams.solve() function, which solves the problem with default options, or by specifying a solver and corresponding options as described here here

docs.title: Helper Functions
docs.text: These helper functions set all necessary parameterss to define the problem. They define some common usage patterns for optimization, such as fully optimized waveforms that start and end at 0 (vec_init_simple), or the optimization of diffusion waveforms (diff_init).

diff_init(dt: float = 0.0004, TE: float = 0.08, T_90: float = 0.003, T_180: float = 0.005, T_readout: float = 0.016)

Initialize diffusion sequence parameters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dt float

Raster time in seconds.

0.0004 TE float

Echo time in seconds.

0.08 T_90 float

Duration of the excitation RF pulse in seconds. This should only include the time from excitation, so half of the full RF pulse duration.

0.003 T_180 float

Duration of the refocusing RF pulse in seconds.

0.005 T_readout float

Time to TE of the readout in seconds.

0.016

docs.title: Direct Setup
docs.text:
The individual components of the problem definition are:

Name Description N The number of points of the wave form, per-axis Naxis Number of axis dt Gradient raster time [seconds] set_vec A vector that contains either gradient values or NaN, which describes if a given point in the waveform has a fixed value, or is optimizable (NaN) inv_vec A vector of either 1 or -1 describing which points of the waveform have been RF inverted X0 An initial guess at the solution waveform

Many of these wll be automatically generated for the simplest options if omitted.

docs.title: setvec_X0
docs.text:
setvec_X0(X0: ndarray, set_others: bool = True)

Set the initial waveform guess.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default X0 ndarray

Initial guess for the waveform (warm start). [T/m]

required set_others bool

If True, other related vectors (inv_vec, set_vals, fixer) will be updated with standard values.

True

docs.title: set_general_params
docs.text:
set_general_params(min_iter: int = 1, max_iter: int = 2000, log_interval: int = 20, gamma_x: float = 1.6, max_feval: int = 12000)

Set general parameters for the SDMM solver.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_iter int

Minimum number of iterations for the main SDMM loop. The solver will run for at least this many iterations. Defaults to 1.

1 max_iter int

Maximum number of iterations for the main SDMM loop. Defaults to 2000.

2000 log_interval int

Interval at which to log the progress of the solver. This will only be seen when verbose logging is enabled. Defaults to 20.

20 gamma_x float

Relaxation parameter for the SDMM update step. correspond to over-relaxation, which can speed up convergence. Defaults to 1.6.

1.6

docs.title: set_ils_params
docs.text:
set_ils_params(ils_tol: float = 0.001, ils_max_iter: int = 20, ils_min_iter: int = 2, ils_sigma: float = 0.0001, ils_tik_lam: float = 0.0)

Set parameters for the indirect linear solver used in the SDMM.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ils_tol float

Relative tolerance for the inner-loop indirect linear solver (e.g., CG). The ILS stops when the residual norm is less than ils_tol times the initial residual norm. Defaults to 1e-3.

0.001 ils_max_iter int

Maximum number of iterations for the indirect linear solver per main SDMM iteration. Defaults to 20.

20 ils_min_iter int

Minimum number of iterations for the indirect linear solver. Defaults to 2.

2 ils_sigma float

Regularization parameter for the linear system solved in the inner loop, related to the ADMM penalty parameter. Defaults to 1e-4.

0.0001 ils_tik_lam float

Tikhonov (L2) regularization parameter for the indirect linear solver. Adds a penalty on the norm of the solution to improve conditioning. Defaults to 0.0.

0.0

docs.title: set_sdmm_params
docs.text:
set_sdmm_params(rw_interval: int = 8, rw_e_corr: float = 0.4, rw_eps: float = 1e-36, rw_scalelim: float = 1.5, grw_min_infeasible: int = 20, grw_interval: int = 20, grw_mod: float = 2.0)

Set parameters specific to the SDMM algorithm.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rw_interval int

Interval for reweighting operations. Defaults to 8.

8 rw_e_corr float

Error correction parameter for reweighting. Defaults to 0.4.

0.4 rw_eps float

Small epsilon value for numerical stability in reweighting. Defaults to 1e-36.

1e-36 rw_scalelim float

Scale limit for reweighting operations. Defaults to 1.5.

1.5 grw_min_infeasible int

Minimum number of infeasible iterations before adaptive reweighting is allowed. Defaults to 20.

20 grw_interval int

Interval for adaptive reweighting checks. Defaults to 20.

20 grw_mod float

Modification factor for adaptive reweighting. Defaults to 2.0.

2.0

docs.title: solve
docs.text:
solve(gparams)

Run the SDMM solver.

Uses the problem definitions set during the initialization of the solver.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: \[ \begin{aligned} & \underset{x}{\text{minimize}} & & \dfrac{1}{2} x^T P x + q^T x \\ & \text{subject to} & & l \leq Ax \leq u \\ % & & & f_i(x) \leq b_i, \; i = 1, \ldots, m. \end{aligned} \]

docs.title: Residuals
docs.text: \[ r_{prim} = Ax - z \] \[ r_{dual} = Px + q + A^Ty \]

docs.title: Indirect Linear Solver
docs.text: \[ (P + \sigma I + \rho A^T A)\tilde{x}^{k+1} = \sigma x^{k} - q + A^T(\rho z^k - y^k) \] \[ \tilde{z}^{k+1} = A \tilde{x}^{k+1} \]

docs.title: rho Balancing
docs.text: \[ \rho^{k+1} = \rho^{k} \sqrt{      \frac{\left\Vert r_{prim}^k \right\Vert _{\infty} / \, \textrm{max} \{ \left\Vert Ax^k \right\Vert _{\infty}, \left\Vert z^k \right\Vert _{\infty}  \} }     {\left\Vert r_{dual}^k \right\Vert _{\infty} / \,  \textrm{max} \{ \left\Vert Px^k \right\Vert _{\infty}, \left\Vert A^Ty^k \right\Vert _{\infty}, \left\Vert q \right\Vert _{\infty}  \} }     } \]
